sources.title: GCU Bachelor of Science in Business Administration — current official program curriculum and course prerequisites
sources.scope: Program states campus and online availability, 120 semester credits, 64-credit major and 34–40 general education / 16–22 elective ranges. The sixteen named major courses each carry four credits. Program page academic approval date: September 15, 2026.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 Academic Catalog — BS Business Administration
sources.scope: Printed pages 61–62: all sixteen required four-credit major courses, 64 major credits, 34–40 general education, 16–22 electives and 120 total. BUS-340 and BUS-485 carry the writing-intensive designation.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 Academic Catalog — Bachelor of Science general education
sources.scope: Printed pages 54–56 list the five general education competencies and named GCU course choices. BS ranges: foundations 4, communication 9–12, worldview 4, critical thinking 11–12, global awareness 6–8. UNV-103/303 and CWV-101/301 are marked non-transferable in the published sequence; campus students can have additional approved choices.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 Academic Catalog — named unrestricted elective selections
sources.scope: The BSBA has an open elective allowance. INT-244, COM-100, SOC-102 and SOC-220 are actual named four-credit university courses. They are selected examples, not additional required major courses or a promise of registration availability.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 University Policy Handbook — baccalaureate transfer policies
sources.scope: Printed pages 261–262: maximum 90 transfer credits, at most 84 lower-division; 30 combined alternative credits; another 30 maximum from military schools/training; all other transfer must be on an accredited GCU-approved originating college transcript. Lower-division substitutions do not become upper-division credit. Undergraduate transfer generally requires C or better; pass grades must equate to C. No duplicate/remedial credit.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 University Policy Handbook — alternative credit source treatment
sources.scope: Printed pages 262–263: combined 30-credit alternative ceiling, source transcript controls testing credit quantity and level; ACE credit is applied by transcript first to matching content/general education then electives. NCCRS may apply to undergraduate lower-division general education or electives. General alternative acceptance is not an exact course equivalency.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 University Policy Handbook — degree credit minimum and transfer shortfalls
sources.scope: Printed page 262 quarter-conversion example preserves 2.67 earned credits toward 120 even when English content is fulfilled. Printed page 267 allows GCU Service Learning coursework to fill a transfer-related shortfall toward 120 in the major/elective categories; Service Learning cannot fulfill general education. Content substitution never establishes a larger credit award.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 University Policy Handbook — bachelor graduation, residency, upper division and writing
sources.scope: Printed pages 267–268: 120 minimum; 30 semester credits at GCU; 36 upper total and at least 36 upper credits in the major; overall and major GPA 2.0, major courses C or better. Three writing-intensive courses include ENG-105/equivalent and two major courses, at least one upper. Traditional campus foundations waiver needs 24 transferred college-level credits and 3.0 GPA.

sources.title: GCU Fall 2026 University Policy Handbook — campus mathematics and English placement
sources.scope: Traditional campus freshmen must take the appropriate placement examination before math above MAT-110. Transfer students need placement unless a C-or-better approved prerequisite transfers from an approved accredited college. Direct ENG-105 registration depends on English competency/placement or the published waiver alternatives. Remedial prerequisites are not counted inside this 120-credit ledger.

models.coverageLabel: Complete campus BSBA requirements with current Sophia and ASU transfer choices, actual earned-credit accounting and sourced category allocations.

curriculumAllocation.scope: The selected native-course baseline uses 40 general education plus 64 major plus 16 open electives. Published ranges permit a different transfer-credit allocation; they do not award unearned credits or waive 120 total.

institutionMinCredits.scope: Explicit bachelor residency: at least 30 semester credits of coursework in a GCU program. This value is not inferred from the 90-credit transfer ceiling.

externalMaxCredits.scope: Overall undergraduate transfer ceiling; individual applicability and the remaining graduation requirements still constrain actual use.

alternativeMaxCredits.scope: One combined ceiling across alternative sources, not 30 per provider. Military-school/training credit has its separately stated ceiling and still counts toward the overall transfer limit.

upperMinCredits.scope: At least 36 semester credits in 300-or-higher courses; Major/Core also requires at least 36 upper-division credits in the major.

gradePolicy.detail: Undergraduate transfer generally requires C or better; pass grades must equate to C. Major coursework requires C or better; the student must maintain overall and major GPA 2.0. This does not assert a blanket C floor for every native elective.

transferPolicyReview.residencyNote: At least 30 semester credits must be earned in a GCU program; 36 upper credits in the major must remain satisfied independently of content substitutions.

degreeCreditBalancePolicy.shortfallMechanism: GCU Service Learning coursework may fill a transfer-related credit shortfall in the major/elective category. Specific eligible service-learning course, credit amount and applicability must be independently established before generating a transfer scenario.
degreeCreditBalancePolicy.note: A receiving-course content match is not evidence that a 3-credit source earns 4 degree credits. Preserve the actual transcript quantity and level; an exact transfer scenario must separately reach 120, the general education minima and 36 upper-major credits.

degreeCreditBalancePolicy.noteOnCandidates: Current official course identities are research inputs, not additional requirements inside the native 120-credit ledger. Each listed identity is distinct. foundationsWaiver.note: Traditional campus students meeting both conditions can waive University Foundations. The waiver does not create earned credits or reduce the 120-credit degree minimum; this baseline retains the course.

writingIntensiveRule.transferTreatment: A content-equivalent outside course must separately satisfy the writing-intensive graduation requirement; the receiving-course label alone does not establish the source designation. Retain the native major options unless a reviewed equivalent designation or a separately researched replacement meets the rule.

graduationRequirements.title: Overall and major GPA
graduationRequirements.description: At least 2.0 overall and major GPA; no grade below C may count toward the major.

graduationRequirements.title: Writing-intensive coursework
graduationRequirements.description: Complete at least three designated writing-intensive courses: ENG-105 or its equivalent and two in the major, at least one upper division. The selected native baseline includes ENG-105, ENG-106, BUS-340 and BUS-485.

graduationRequirements.title: Campus mathematics and English placement
graduationRequirements.description: Meet the campus placement/approved-prerequisite conditions before registering in MAT-144 and ENG-105. Any needed developmental preparation is separate from the 120 degree-credit ledger.

rulesNotes: Selected native allocation: 40 general education + 64 required major + 16 open electives = 120 semester credits; no requirement is counted twice.
The required major is the current sixteen-course 64-credit BSBA. ACC-250/ACC-260 are not inferred substitutes for its current ACC-240 requirement.
General education course choices and open electives are selections within published competencies/allowances, not claims that every student must take these exact electives.
Lower-division transfer can satisfy the content of an upper-division course but cannot satisfy upper-division credit minima. Major upper-division credit is a separate 36-credit rule.
Published transfer ceilings are not course-level awards. No Sophia, Study.com, CLEP, NCCRS or institutional-equivalency option is fabricated by this curriculum importer.
Campus transfer foundations waivers require both 24 college-level credits and 3.0 GPA. The baseline does not assume either personal eligibility fact.
Registration offerings, individual admission/catalog assignment and personal transfer evaluation remain institution-controlled; no graduation date or tuition estimate is invented.
Each reviewed Sophia content option counts three actual semester credits against a four-credit native requirement. The proposed plan independently balances earned credits to at least 120.

BUS-340 and BUS-485 remain native writing-intensive major courses. Available outside options are choices; residency, category minima, upper-major credits and the six-credit unique Service Learning pool constrain the selected mix.

ASU Universal Learner choices use actual university-issued semester credits. Category awards are proposed within the sourced BSBA allowance and are not named-course equivalencies. ASU on-demand choices require at least six weeks; the scheduled chemistry alternative is labeled separately.
